As we wrap up, I want you to remember this—if you’ve ever felt that quiet exhaustion from invisible labor, or maybe the sting of being taken for granted, you’re absolutely not alone. The journey we’ve walked through *Fed Up!* is one so many of us share—often quietly, often without recognition. But what these stories remind us is that there’s always a way forward. A way that’s built on honesty, on community, and on the courage to ask for what you truly need.
So, here’s what I hope you’ll carry with you: Even the smallest act of sharing the load can spark real, lasting change at home. When you lean on community and solidarity, invisible work gets lighter—and a whole lot more visible. Letting go of perfect? That opens up space for joy, for rest, and for real connection with the people you love. And self-advocacy—it’s not just a one-and-done thing. It’s a practice. So, keep showing up for yourself, even on the hard days. Real, lasting change? It’s built on the little choices you make each day, not some grand gesture or quick fix. The work of caring—your work—is valuable, even when it goes unseen. You deserve recognition, support, and the chance to rest without any guilt. If you ever find yourself slipping back into old habits, be gentle with yourself. Change isn’t a straight line, and setbacks are just part of the process. Reach out. Share your story. Invite those around you to help carry the weight. Every conversation, every healthy boundary, every act of self-care—it all adds up to a more equitable, more fulfilling life. You’re not in this alone. The invisible work you do matters—and so do you. With each small shift, you’re helping build a world where everyone is seen, valued, and supported. So keep going. The journey is worth it, and you are more than enough.
